proposed_reports.title: Property Assessment Notices and Roll (Service New Brunswick Property Assessment)
proposed_reports.description: Annual real property assessments at market value for all properties in New Brunswick under the Assessment Act, delivered as Property Assessment Notices and used by the province and local governments to set property tax rates and levies.

proposed_reports.title: 2026 Budget Paper on the Economy
proposed_reports.publisher: Department of Finance and Affordability, Government of Prince Edward Island
proposed_reports.description: Supporting economic outlook document published with the 2026-27 operating budget, providing the growth, inflation and other assumptions underlying the fiscal forecasts.

dependencies.basis: The 2026-2027 Estimates of Revenue and Expenditures explicitly list Equalization as a line under Revenue from Government of Canada, with the Budget Estimate of $722,707,000 for the fiscal year commencing 1 April 2026.
The Estimates list Canada Health Transfer as a distinct federal revenue line for 2026-2027.
The Estimates list Canada Social Transfer as a distinct federal revenue line for 2026-2027.

The Budget 2026-27 revenue outlook states Nova Scotia’s Equalization entitlement estimate for 2026–27 is $3.5 billion and records Equalization Payments under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources; the program grows with the three-year average of national nominal GDP.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Nova Scotia’s entitlement estimate for 2026–27 is $3.5 billion, an increase of $73.6 million or 2.1 per cent compared to the 2025–26 Budget Estimates... The Equalization program is legislated to grow by the three-year average growth rate of national nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP). For 2026–27 the growth rate is 3.79 per cent and the national funding pool for distribution is $27.2 billion.

dependencies.basis: Budget 2026-27 records the Canada Health Transfer under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources with the 2026-27 estimate of $1,507,399 thousand.
Budget 2026-27 records the Canada Social Transfer under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources with the 2026-27 estimate of $470,934 thousand.
The Statements and Schedules 2026 accompanying the Estimates list Equalization as a distinct Government of Canada revenue component for 2026-27 (approximately $182 million).
